title: No per-session rate cap: holder credentials meet only one tenant-wide, cluster-global limit

story.i_want_to: never have a legitimate message or read refused because my own key hit a per-key cap
story.so_that: coordination works hardest exactly when it matters most, while one tenant-wide bound still stops a runaway fleet

rationale: Mark (PRD R11): 'I trust agents enough that they'd avoid any abuses.' Today every limit is per key, and under R3 a key is a session: the API pipeline allows rate_limit_requests_per_minute (default 300) per key and derives the tenant bound as three times that (lib/loopctl_web/plugs/rate_limiter.ex:37, :53-54), and the coordination controllers add their own per-key caps: channel posts 120 writes and 240 reads a minute (channel_post_controller.ex:146, :154), locks 120 (channel_lock_controller.ex:92) and claims 60 writes and 120 reads (channel_claim_controller.ex:136, :141). The tenant bound is counted on the node-local Hammer limiter unless RATE_LIMITER=postgres (config/runtime.exs:45-47), so it grows with the node count release 10 adds.

acceptance_criteria.description: LoopctlWeb.Plugs.RateLimiter makes no per-key check for an api key carrying a holder_id; the response's x-ratelimit-limit and x-ratelimit-remaining then report the tenant-wide bucket.
A key without a holder_id keeps today's per-key check against the tenant setting rate_limit_requests_per_minute (default 300), and a superadmin key stays exempt from both checks.

The tenant-wide limit is the tenant setting rate_limit_tenant_requests_per_minute (default 900), no longer per_key_limit * 3: a tenant that set rate_limit_requests_per_minute to 100 keeps a tenant limit of 900.

The tenant bucket is counted on Loopctl.RateLimiter.Postgres whatever RATE_LIMITER selects, resolved through Loopctl.RateLimiter.tenant_impl/0 (config DI, default Postgres), so requests served by two nodes draw on one budget.

The per-key coordination caps are deleted with their settings and plugs: rate_limit_write and rate_limit_read in ChannelPostController (channel_post_write_limit_per_minute, channel_post_read_limit_per_minute), rate_limit_lock in ChannelLockController (channel_lock_limit_per_minute) and rate_limit_claim and rate_limit_claim_read in ChannelClaimController; the 121st channel write in a minute from one holder credential succeeds.

A tenant over its limit gets 429 with retry-after and the {error: {status: 429, message: "Rate limit exceeded"}} body, and a limiter fault (raise, exit or throw) still fails open with one throttled FailOpenLog line.

The OpenAPI RateLimitError description (lib/loopctl/api_spec/schemas.ex:143) names the tenant setting and says holder credentials have no per-key limit; CHANGELOG.md records the removed caps, the new setting and its default.

test_cases.name: per-key check skipped for a holder credential only (ConnCase, plugs/rate_limiter_test.exs)
preconditions: tenant settings rate_limit_requests_per_minute 2, rate_limit_tenant_requests_per_minute 100; a holder credential (US-52.13); a plain agent key; a superadmin key; the injected limiter mock from config/test.exs
steps: 3 requests with the plain agent key
expected_results: holder: three 200s and x-ratelimit-limit 100; plain: 200, 200, 429; superadmin: no limiter call

test_cases.name: tenant limit decoupled from the per-key setting (unit, plug with a stubbed limiter)
preconditions: tenant settings rate_limit_requests_per_minute 100 and no tenant setting; a second tenant with rate_limit_tenant_requests_per_minute 50
steps: call the plug for each tenant and capture the limit passed for the tenant: bucket
expected_results: 900 for the first tenant, 50 for the second

test_cases.name: tenant bucket shared across nodes on Postgres (DataCase, async: false: a committed counter row two connections share, moduledoc says why)
preconditions: rate_limit_tenant_requests_per_minute 3; :rate_limiter left at Hammer; Loopctl.Test.ProductionTopology for a second connection
steps: two requests through the plug on connection 1 and two on connection 2, both stamped as different nodes
expected_results: the fourth request is 429; the rate_limit_counters row for tenant:<id> counts 4

test_cases.name: coordination caps gone (ConnCase)
preconditions: holder credential that is a writable member; tenant limit 1000
steps: grep the controllers for rate_limit_ plugs (unit assertion on the plug list)
expected_results: no 429 among them; none of the three controllers declares a rate plug

test_cases.name: 429 shape and fail-open (unit, plug)
preconditions: a limiter stub returning {:deny, 900}; one raising; one exiting
expected_results: 429 with retry-after >= 1 and the error body; then two pass-throughs and one FailOpenLog warning per bucket family

technical_notes: Plug: lib/loopctl_web/plugs/rate_limiter.ex call/2 :52-75, get_per_key_limit/1 :116-120, check_rate/2 :85-96 (fail-open :98-105). Holder id: conn.assigns.current_api_key.holder_id (api_keys.holder_id, provided by US-52.13). The plug is mounted in the :authenticated pipeline (router.ex:53).

Limiter seam: Loopctl.RateLimiter.impl/0 (lib/loopctl/rate_limiter.ex:63) keeps serving every other gate; add tenant_impl/0 reading Application.get_env(:loopctl, :tenant_rate_limiter, Loopctl.RateLimiter.Postgres). Loopctl.RateLimiter.Postgres.check_rate/3 (lib/loopctl/rate_limiter/postgres.ex:132) fails open itself; the plug's own rescue stays for the stub case. Per CLAUDE.md, tests never Application.put_env: the plug takes the limiter as an init opt defaulting to tenant_impl/0, and tests pass the mock.
Cost (config/runtime.exs:36-44): the Postgres impl runs one upsert on AdminRepo per authenticated request; only the tenant bucket goes there, the per-key bucket for non-holder keys stays on impl/0.

Deleted code: channel_post_controller.ex:94-117 (plugs), :140-159 (defaults), :1375-1521 (rate functions, settings reads, pipeline clamp); channel_lock_controller.ex:77-95, :334-400; channel_claim_controller.ex:118-155, :502-620; and their 429 entries in each operation/2 (e.g. channel_post_controller.ex:183, :262, :338). The coordination :rate_limited security event and limit_kind token (channel_post_controller.ex:1551-1568) go with them.

Other readers of rate_limit_requests_per_minute stay unchanged: LoopctlWeb.Plugs.AuthPathThrottle (auth_path_throttle.ex:99) and CorpusController's per-item charge (corpus_controller.ex:1185-1212) are not coordination caps.

Setting docs: tenant settings are free-form (Tenants.get_tenant_settings/3, tenants.ex:1191); document rate_limit_tenant_requests_per_minute in the Schemas.RateLimitError text and CHANGELOG.md (CLAUDE.md, Doc hygiene: API constraint). No env var is added.
non_goals: Per-key limits for runner, orchestrator and user keys: unchanged.
The security throttles (signup, WebAuthn, enroll, AuthPathThrottle): unchanged; they guard abuse, not coordination.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.26.6: when the limiter's database is unreachable the check fails open, so a partitioned limiter never blocks the fleet; the outage is logged once per bucket family per window.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.26.4: the tenant count lives in rate_limit_counters in Postgres, shared by every node, so a node restart or a second region neither resets nor multiplies the budget.
failure_modes.retry: n/a: the limiter counts requests and a retried request is a request; nothing it counts is a write that could apply twice.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.26.6: a limiter call that exits (pool checkout timeout) fails open, so a slow counter table delays nothing past the pool timeout.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: an inline plug in the request process.

definition_of_done: On production: a holder credential sends 130 channel messages in one minute with no 429; SELECT count FROM rate_limit_counters WHERE bucket = 'tenant:<tenant id>' ORDER BY window_start DESC LIMIT 1 shows the tenant count growing.
defaults: Tenant-wide limit: 900 requests a minute (rate_limit_tenant_requests_per_minute), today's derived value at the default per-key limit (owner may change).
The per-key coordination caps on locks and claims are removed with the two channel-post caps, because they are the same per-key class.
